A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ResGS and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete four-page supplements. Retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and repeated-run results on Mip-NeRF360, Tanks&Temples, and Deep Blending.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds Waymo evaluation, random-initialization comparisons, and Deep Blending component ablations.

M1.justification: Residual Gaussian creation, opacity reduction, image-pyramid supervision, level-dependent densification thresholds, and losses remain unchanged. The inconsistent change from training to rendering in the description of l_i does not establish a new procedure: the threshold rule and training diagram retain its original role.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on large-scale urban scenes from Waymo in Section 6.1 and Table 5. This extends dataset coverage within novel view synthesis; the three original datasets and task remain.

E2.justification: GaussianPro, previously discussed only as related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in the new Waymo comparison. Existing comparison tables retain their baseline membership. The random-initialization study uses six already-evaluated Gaussian-splatting baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6.4 introduces a controlled initialization comparison using the same random point clouds across methods, with SfM-initialized ResGS as a reference. Existing main-experiment splits, resolutions, metrics, model variants, and stated training budgets remain. The new Waymo evaluation supplies little additional protocol information.

E4.justification: v3 adds a substantial robustness study of dependence on SfM initialization across all three original datasets and six baselines (Table 11). Table 4 also extends component ablations to Deep Blending, testing whether pyramid supervision helps in weakly textured scenes. Existing compatibility, hyperparameter-sensitivity, and opacity-reduction analyses remain.

E5.justification: The ten-run averages and population standard deviations in v2 Tables 5–7 are retained unchanged in v3 Tables 6–8. No additional seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover urban scenes, initialization dependence, and component interactions. Waymo PSNR is 35.29 for ResGS versus 34.68 for GaussianPro, while LPIPS ties at 0.191. Random initialization yields ResGS PSNR 26.38 on Mip-NeRF360 versus 28.00 with SfM. The added Deep Blending ablation reports 29.05 for Base+IP versus 29.60 for Base. Existing matched results remain unchanged; these are added experimental conditions, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The eight displayed equations retain their substantive mathematical content. Renaming the image-pyramid notation and expanding the coordinate description do not introduce new theory. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its positioning claim from previous approaches having not modified densification to their seldom adapting it. The central claims about adaptive residual split, coarse-to-fine training, rendering quality, and compatibility with other pipelines remain.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3.2–4.4 replace the earlier stage-dependent split/clone explanation with an overfitting account for weakly textured Deep Blending scenes. v3 claims implicit control of Gaussian counts but identifies missing explicit regularization as a limitation. The new initialization discussion acknowledges dependence on SfM. The earlier occlusion/overfitting caveat remains in the supplement.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link but removes v2's specification of a 500-iteration inter-stage warm-up with densification disabled. This reduces implementation detail without establishing that the actual training procedure changed. Most hyperparameters, loss information, and RTX3090 hardware disclosure remain.

R1.justification: v3 removes the MVGS citation and BARF discussion, adds references for Waymo and Structure-from-Motion Revisited, and softens the novelty positioning concerning earlier densification methods. Numerous other bibliography edits update metadata for retained works rather than introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: v3 edits the introduction and method explanations, rewrites the ablation and limitations discussion, retitles Section 4, and adds acknowledgements and two supplementary subsections. Affiliation and corresponding-author information also change. The overall narrative and main section organization remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds Waymo and random-initialization tables, expands Table 4 with Deep Blending columns, and relocates retained supplementary tables. Figures 1–3 receive illustration or label refinements, and Figure 7 changes proportions while retaining its sensitivity trend. The overall visual organization remains recognizable.

improvement.justification: The initialization study and expanded ablation make the evidence more informative by exposing SfM dependence and a failure of pyramid-only supervision that v2 did not test. Waymo adds evidence of broader applicability. These gains are limited by sparse descriptions of the new experimental settings, removal of the warm-up detail, and the Waymo prose claiming improvement on every metric despite tied LPIPS. The net improvement is useful but bounded.
